name: Study abroad term
one_line: The organizational situation of studying for a term or a year at a host institution while remaining enrolled at a home institution: two institutions occupy one school field at once, the coursework arrives in another language and another course-numbering shape, and the branch's administrative spine — nomination, learning agreement, enrollment certificate, credit-transfer approval — sits beside immigration, housing and travel material that must be detected and protected rather than filed here.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key_works: The canonical row for school reads 'the institution the holder attends, attended, or teaches at - the person's own school, never the application target'. In this situation the holder attends TWO institutions at the same time in two different roles: the home institution of record, which awards the credit and issues the transfer approval, and the host institution of study, which teaches the courses and issues the transcript of records. target_university is the wrong key because after placement nothing is being applied to; the holder is enrolled at both. Under a single school key a learning agreement that names both institutions in two separately labelled table rows cannot say which value plays which role, and a folder dimension built on school cannot keep host coursework apart from home administration. 00 states the rule this proposal is an instance of: "The system must separate roles that happen to contain the same entity type." Its own example is the neighbouring one: "An application essay can mention the author’s current school and the university to which the essay is addressed. Those are not the same field." Rule family for the ceiling: a schools-gazetteer hit matched at a word boundary sitting in a labelled host/exchange slot, or in exchange-program context that names it as the receiving institution - never a second university name on its own.
proposed_fields.not_authored_here: This node does not write the key into canonical_fields.json and does not put it in dimension_order, because a dimension may only branch on a field the schema declares. The cheaper alternative R1c may prefer is recorded in open_question and in the research notes: keep one school field, let it carry two values on one file, and leave the role to the evidence location - which costs the folder dimension its ability to separate them.

deterministic: an exchange-program context term in a high-weight zone (filename, document title, page-one heading) - study abroad, exchange, host institution, home institution, learning agreement, transcript of records, credit transfer, visiting student, semester abroad - co-occurring with a schools-gazetteer hit matched at a word boundary. The program term is what carries the situation; the institution name never does, because 00 forbids it alone: "A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization."

two distinct schools-gazetteer hits inside one document occupying two separately labelled slots whose labels name opposite roles (a table row labelled Home institution beside one labelled Host institution; Sending and Receiving; Study abroad office beside a partner university). The labelled cell is what makes the roles readable at all - 00: "Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs." Two bare university names in running prose are not this signal.

a course-equivalency table: rows that pair a course-code-shaped token from one institution with a course-code-shaped token or credit count from another, on a document whose issuing heading names a registrar or study-abroad office. This is the credit-transfer signature and it is the one shape that evidences both school values from one file.

a dedicated academic-term pattern co-occurring with an exchange-program context term and a schools-gazetteer hit, including the academic-year shape - 00: "Academic terms such as Spring 2025, AY 2024-25, and Michaelmas Term 2024 require dedicated patterns rather than generic parsing." A full-year exchange is the case that keeps term worth extracting even though this template does not branch on it.

an enrollment or attendance certificate whose labelled slots name a host institution, a program start and end date, and a credit or hour load, issued for presentation to a third party - the shape a visa application consumes. It evidences school and term; the identity material it sits beside is not this template's to hold.

a curated existing parent folder whose own name carries an exchange-program term or a host-institution token, together with at least one member file that independently clears one of the rules above. Folder context is a clue needing an in-file anchor, and 00 requires existing structure be read rather than rewritten: "The system learns from existing folders but must not silently reorganize them."
needs_llm: which of two institution names in one document is the home one and which is the host, when both appear only in prose and neither sits in a labelled slot. The model must cite the sentence that assigns the role and return unknown otherwise; a wrong answer here silently mislabels the whole branch.

a host-institution syllabus or timetable in a language whose term vocabulary and course-numbering shape the deterministic pattern catalogue does not cover (a.a. 2026-27, Michaelmas, Hilary, trimestre, Wintersemester). 00 names the population: real corpora contain "multilingual documents, screenshots, unlabeled forms", and it forbids the shortcut of judging them by text quality - "The system should not use unreliable global language-quality checks that incorrectly punish multilingual or mathematics-heavy documents."

whether an application-shaped document is an exchange placement inside an existing enrollment or a degree admission to a new institution - the same essay register, the same portal language, a different situation and a different neighbour row.
whether a set of host-institution files is one exchange term or two, when a full academic year abroad produces two terms of coursework under one program name and one agreement.

an unlabelled acceptance or nomination letter whose only signal is prose congratulating the reader on a place at a named institution, where nothing distinguishes an exchange place from an admission offer.
an archive or download whose members mix host coursework, immigration paperwork and travel bookings, where the question is whether one program explains the packet or several unrelated errands do.
never_alone: two university names in one file alone. This is this template's own tempting false file: a host institution named in a running footer, a partner university listed in a course catalogue, a university cited in a bibliography beside the author's own. Role language or a labelled slot must say which institution is home and which is host, and 00's rule applies to each name separately - "A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization."

a foreign or non-domestic institution name alone. Foreignness is not evidence of enrolment: the same name can be a venue, an employer, a co-author's affiliation or a place the holder merely read about.

a foreign city, country or airport token in a filename or path alone. Travel evidence is not enrolment evidence, and 00's own residual worked example refuses exactly this inference - "It must not invent a folder called Travel/Flight Gate B12 or assume that a gate number identifies a particular trip."

a visa, residence permit, passport or national-ID document alone. It evidences identity, never a term of study, and it must not be pulled into an academic branch by proximity: "Finance, identity, medical, and legal material should be implemented first as safety domains, meaning the system detects and protects them before any cloud or automated placement decision is allowed."

a course-code-shaped token in an unfamiliar numbering shape with no academic context describing the document - the ZIP-code and device-model confusion 00 lists in its adversarial suite applies harder abroad, where the local numbering shape is unknown to the pattern catalogue.

a bare 4-digit number, or one half of an academic-year token, as a term - 00 warns of "numbers that look like years but are course identifiers, version numbers, build numbers, ZIP codes, or other unrelated values".

source_type or extension alone: text_document, presentation, calendar, image, ocr and archive membership never make this situation plausible without content evidence, because 00 requires the engine to "treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning".
a same-session download batch of flight, housing, visa and course files as proof that they are one study-abroad program - 00: "A session should never be treated as proof of topic".
a parent folder named Abroad, Erasmus, Exchange or a host-city name alone, with no member file carrying an exchange term plus an institution hit.

a homework- or exercise-shaped filename in the host language alone (esercizio 3.pdf, Aufgabe 3.pdf). It may support work_type and nothing else, exactly as 00's own sparse case does - "The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files."

proposed_context_terms_note: Proposed by this node, not asserted as 00's. 00's five academic context terms - syllabus, lecture, credits, instructor, semester - remain the design floor and reach the schema's subject fact; the terms above are what distinguish this situation from ordinary coursework and are R6's to catalogue, never regexes written here.
work_types_note: Values of the schema's work_type field, never nodes - "The system may create new values when it sees a new course, project, company, university, or event, but it should not invent new fields automatically." The first six are what this situation adds to the coursework list: an exchange branch's administrative spine is made of documents that ordinary coursework never produces, and each of them is a value discovered at runtime rather than a field, a schema or a roster row.
grouping_reasons: one exchange program at one host institution across one term or one academic year - the program, not the course, is what holds the branch together, and a full-year exchange must not be split into two groups merely because two term patterns appear

the home-side administrative chain of one exchange - nomination, learning agreement, enrollment certificate, credit-transfer approval - which is purpose-coherent while being content-incoherent, the shape 00 describes for a packet: "The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent"
one host course across its work types, where a foreign course-numbering token repeats across a syllabus, a reading list and an exam paper
a host-institution neighbourhood in which sparse foreign-language files are context-supported members only - the membership record may exist while no subject fact does

template.why: The schema's default order for coursework is 00's own - "An Academic template may define school → term → course → work type" - and this situation departs from it at exactly one level, which is what licenses the row on the dimension test. A study-abroad branch is, by construction, one host institution and usually one term, so a term level under it produces a single child: 00 tells the canvas to warn on precisely that shape - "It should warn when a level produces only one child, repeats a concept already expressed in the parent, creates excessive depth, or creates a large number of tiny folders" - and to act on it - "It should recommend flattening when a dimension does not materially improve retrieval." term therefore stays a fact and stops being a folder level here. The optional branch pattern that restores it is the full-academic-year exchange, where two terms of host coursework sit under one program and one agreement; 00 explicitly permits the unevenness - "The product should not force every branch to use the full template or have the same number of levels", and "each branch should offer the dimensions that are actually present in its member groups and show what each split would create." What survives from the default is the parent-context rule, unchanged: "A work type such as Homework 3 is meaningful only after the course is known, and a course code may require the school or term to disambiguate it" - so subject still precedes work_type, and school still leads because it is the value that makes a foreign course code intelligible. instructor is excluded because it is not destination-eligible: "It should avoid using authorship or creator identity as a destination dimension." The branch's administrative spine carries no subject at all, which is what the scoped fallback is for - "the future tree can include Academics/Columbia/2026-Spring/General rather than sending it to a global Unsorted folder." The leading school value is the HOST institution; the home institution's own credit-transfer paperwork carries the home value in the same field and would land in a different branch under this order - the unresolved consequence recorded in proposed_fields and open_question. All of this is a recommendation and none of it is a path: "The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions."

collides_with.signal: Identical evidence on the coursework side: a course-code-shaped token plus an academic context term, a term pattern, a work-type term. The discriminating evidence is the exchange-program context term plus a second institution in a labelled or role-marked slot; without it the file is home coursework. A foreign course-numbering shape, a foreign language, or a foreign institution name discriminates nothing on its own. Fixture: Syllabus BUSIB 4300 Spring 2026.pdf sits on the coursework side of this seam; 27991_Storia_Contemporanea_aa2026-27.pdf sits on this side only once an exchange anchor exists in its neighbourhood, and even then it carries no subject of its own.

A host transcript of records is an official academic record and reads identically from either side: registrar language, a seal caption, a verification code, a table of many course rows. The discriminating evidence: this template's situation needs an exchange or host/home role marker tying the record to one program of study; the credentials situation is the general case of an official record with no such marker, and no single subject or term value describes either file. Fixture: Transcript of Records - Universita di Bologna.pdf.

One evidence item - a host institution named on a document that also carries a passport number, a program date range and a consular addressee - supports both readings, and the cost of getting it wrong is protection, not filing. The discriminating evidence: a document whose function is to authorise entry or residence (permit class, issuing government authority, visa category, passport number as the subject of the document) is immigration material; a document whose function is to state enrolment (institution, term, credit load, registrar issuer) is this template's. Where both are present, 00's ordering decides: "Finance, identity, medical, and legal material should be implemented first as safety domains, meaning the system detects and protects them before any cloud or automated placement decision is allowed." Fixture: Certificate of Enrollment for Visa Application.pdf.

Both sides carry a target institution, a portal, a deadline and essay-shaped prose. The discriminating evidence: an exchange placement is applied for from inside an existing enrolment and names a home institution, a coordinator or a credit arrangement; a degree admission names an admissions cycle and no home enrolment of record. Neither may take a bare university name, and 00 requires the separation to hold downstream too - "an application packet does not silently absorb a document with a conflicting target institution". Fixture: Screenshot 2026-03-14 at 09.12.44.png, which legitimately carries both fact sets on disjoint evidence.

Flights, rail tickets and hotel confirmations arrive in the same download session and often the same folder as the exchange paperwork, and both sides carry a foreign city and a date range. The discriminating evidence: a booking carries a reference number, a passenger or guest name and a transactional layout, and evidences no institution; this template needs an institution plus an exchange marker. The session that brought them together is a retrieval clue only - "A session should never be treated as proof of topic". Fixture: eticket_MXP_2026-09-01.pdf.

Host-city housing sits inside the same program in a person's mind and inside the same folder on disk. The discriminating evidence: a tenancy agreement carries parties, rent, deposit and a term of months and names no institution; a university residence contract that does name the host institution still turns on its own function - accommodation, not study - and takes no subject, work_type or academic term. Fixture: contratto_locazione_via_zamboni.pdf.

A mobility grant letter carries the home institution, the program name and the term alongside an amount, a payment schedule and an account slot. The discriminating evidence: the money side is evidenced by an amount, a disbursement schedule, an account or a tax reference; this template's side by enrolment, courses or credit. The two co-occur on one document routinely, so the item that must not count twice is the institution-plus-program-name pair. Fixture: Erasmus Grant Award Letter.pdf.

also_holds_with_note: Empty by contract, not by finding. CONNECTION.md's closed vocabulary joins also_holds_with between schemas only, and this row is a template; the co-holdings this situation actually produces are asserted on the academic schema row (academic <-> college_applications, academic <-> photos) or belong to pairs that row must decide (academic <-> identity for a visa-facing enrollment certificate, academic <-> finance for a mobility grant letter). Both of those are recorded in the research notes as findings for R1c, since a template may not author a schema-level edge.

falls_through_to.why: 00's own description fits the exchange branch's administrative leftovers exactly - "standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group". Fixtures: Learning Agreement - Bologna Exchange 2026-27.pdf, Transcript of Records - Universita di Bologna.pdf, Credit Transfer Approval - Registrar.pdf, exchange_packet.zip and Erasmus Grant Award Letter.pdf when no exchange group is accepted.

This is the residual home this situation needs that ordinary coursework does not. 00 defines it for "sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials", says such a home "should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts", and licenses surfacing it alone - "Rare but sensitive files such as passports, visas, and legal documents may be surfaced as protected records even when they do not meet a normal group-size threshold." Fixture: Certificate of Enrollment for Visa Application.pdf.

00 defines it for "isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents" - the travel and booking material that arrives with an exchange and evidences no institution. Fixture: eticket_MXP_2026-09-01.pdf.

00 defines it for "papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association" - a downloaded host-institution course catalogue or reading-list chapter whose course never resolves. Fixture: 27991_Storia_Contemporanea_aa2026-27.pdf.

00: "files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision" - the sparse foreign-language exercise where work_type resolved and nothing else did. Fixtures: esercizio 3.pdf, Orientation Week - International Students.ics.
a portal screenshot whose OCR yields no institution has "no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship". Fixture: Screenshot 2026-03-14 at 09.12.44.png when its OCR is unusable.

a campus or whiteboard photograph with camera EXIF and no readable text has "no event, project, reference collection, or photo-family association" on the academic side. Fixture: IMG_3390.HEIC before OCR resolves anything.

role_split.why: Same entity type, different role: the institution the holder is enrolled at versus the institution an application is addressed to. The pair is already recorded in the canonical field list, so this row references it rather than minting it. It matters here because an exchange-placement application briefly makes the host institution a target before it becomes a school, and the fact set changes when the placement is granted.

PROPOSED, not canonical - host_school does not exist in canonical_fields.json and this node does not write it there. Recorded as a role_split candidate because it is the same entity type in a different role (the institution of record versus the institution of study), which 00 makes the test: "The system must separate roles that happen to contain the same entity type." Until R1c or Joseph rules, no dimension branches on it and no fact is written to it; the neighbour named is the coursework template because that is the row whose school value would otherwise absorb both.

sensitivity_why: 00 counts this material in the corpus it protects: the product "processes a highly personal corpus that can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records." This situation is unusual in how many of those it collects at once: an exchange produces educational records, immigration paperwork, a housing agreement, a grant with an account slot, and geotagged captures, all within one program and usually one folder. The privacy rule that differs from ordinary coursework is therefore an ordering rule rather than a grading one - the neighbouring safety material must be detected and protected before this template is offered as a home, because "Finance, identity, medical, and legal material should be implemented first as safety domains, meaning the system detects and protects them before any cloud or automated placement decision is allowed", and a passport or visa "should enter a protected state immediately". A study-abroad branch must never become the place a passport scan is filed because it sat in the same folder as the learning agreement. Which handling class applies is P7's and is not set here.
open_question: Two institutions occupy one school field at once and nothing in the roster resolves the roles. Fork: (a) admit host_school as a canonical field with a role_split against school, which lets a learning agreement state both roles and lets this template branch on the host value - at the cost of a near-duplicate field, which CONNECTION.md licenses only for a genuine role split; or (b) keep one school field carrying two values on one file and leave the role to the evidence location - cheaper, and consistent with facts being multi-valued, but the folder dimension then cannot keep host coursework apart from home administration, and a credit-transfer approval and the courses it approves land in different branches. A second, smaller fork rides on it: an exchange-placement application is evidenced exactly like a degree admission, so does applications.undergraduate-packet own it until a placement is granted, or does this template own the whole arc? R1c or Joseph decides; this node builds on neither answer.
